description: A 2x2 composite of four secondary-electron SEM micrographs of the fatigue-deformed surfaces of Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C austenitic low-density steel, each panel carrying a black 5 um scale bar at lower right; there are no axes or plots. (a) ST sample, delta-sigma/2 = 180 MPa: long, straight, parallel slip steps intersected by two red arrows labelled "Cross slip" that mark local offsets/step-like wavy slip bands. (b) ST sample, delta-sigma/2 = 315 MPa: a far denser array of closely spaced, wavy, curved striations, with a green dashed line labelled "Kink band" drawn along one undulating band. (c) 600-6 sample, delta-sigma/2 = 180 MPa: broad, widely spaced parallel planar slip bands, with blue dashed cross lines labelled "Slip bands" marking two intersecting slip systems. (d) 600-6 sample, delta-sigma/2 = 315 MPa: the same planar character but as a finer, denser band network, again annotated "Slip bands" with blue dashed intersecting lines. Together the panels argue that solution-treated material accumulates highly localized, irreversible wavy slip and kink bands under cyclic load, whereas the kappa-carbide-bearing 600-6 alloy deforms by uniformly spaced reversible planar slip bands at both stress amplitudes.

observations.observation: The figure is a 2x2 array of SEM micrographs, every panel with a black 5 um scale bar at the lower right; no axes, curves or numeric data are present.
Panel (a) carries two red arrows with the printed text "Cross slip" pointing to local offsets on otherwise straight parallel slip bands.
Panel (b) carries a green dashed line with the printed text "Kink band" drawn along undulating, densely spaced striations.
Panels (c) and (d) each carry blue dashed crossing lines with the printed text "Slip bands", indicating two intersecting slip systems in the 600-6 sample.
The slip-band network in panel (d) appears visibly finer and more closely spaced than the broad bands in panel (c), although no spacing values are printed.
The caption states that ST is shown in (a,b) and 600-6 in (c,d), with (a,c) fatigued at delta-sigma/2 = 180 MPa and (b,d) at 315 MPa.
The citing text states that in the ST sample local wavy slip occurs at 180 MPa, produced by screw dislocations cross slipping after pile-up to form step-like slip bands.
The citing text states that at 315 MPa stress localization in the ST sample becomes more severe and kink bands form, indicating loss of deformability.
The citing text states that the 600-6 sample shows distinct, uniformly spaced slip bands at both 180 MPa and 315 MPa, identified as planar slip bands caused by the "glide plane softening" mechanism.
The citing text states that at 315 MPa the spacing between slip bands in 600-6 decreases and cooperative activation of multiple slip systems accommodates plastic strain more uniformly.

The citing text summarises that intragranular kappa-carbides promote reversible planar slip and thereby enhance the fatigue deformation response of the 600-6 sample at all studied cyclic stress levels.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph of the ST sample fatigued at delta-sigma/2 = 180 MPa, showing straight parallel slip steps with subtle offsets; two red arrows labelled "Cross slip" point to locally stepped slip bands. Black 5 um scale bar.

SEM micrograph of the ST sample fatigued at 315 MPa, showing a dense, closely spaced wavy/undulating striation pattern; a green dashed line labelled "Kink band" is drawn along the undulating bands. Black 5 um scale bar.

SEM micrograph of the 600-6 sample fatigued at 180 MPa, showing broad, widely spaced planar slip bands; blue dashed crossing lines labelled "Slip bands" indicate two intersecting slip systems. Black 5 um scale bar.

SEM micrograph of the 600-6 sample fatigued at 315 MPa, showing a finer, denser network of planar slip bands; blue dashed crossing lines labelled "Slip bands" again mark intersecting slip traces. Black 5 um scale bar.
